definition.note: The attempted genus-1 catenoid: two catenoidal ends plus one handle.  Ruled out by Schoen's characterization of the catenoid.

construction.blocked_by: PROVED NOT TO EXIST -- not merely unbuilt.  A complete, properly immersed minimal surface with two catenoidal ends is the catenoid (R. Schoen), so the catenoid with an inward-grown handle necessarily leaves a gap; Weber files it under Non-Existent Surfaces.
construction.resume: Nothing to build as a finite surface.  Growing the handle outward instead yields the periodic fence of catenoids, which already has a record (fence-of-catenoids-karcher).

provenance.definition: Not transcribed. The record exists to state that the surface is absent and why; a fabricated equation would be worse than a null.
sources: M. Weber, 'Translation Invariant Catenoid (which documents the failed inward-handle construction)', minimalsurfaces.blog (local mirror: minsurf/book/.../ch170_translation_invariant_catenoid.md).
M. Weber, 'Non-Existent Surfaces (section index)', minimalsurfaces.blog (local mirror: minsurf/book/.../ch061_non_existent_surfaces.md).
R. Schoen, 'Uniqueness, symmetry, and embeddedness of minimal surfaces', J. Differential Geom. 18 (1983) 791-809.
